correctness.rationale: The binomial survival reward f_q(d)=1-q^d-d(1-q)q^(d-1) has exact discrete derivative Δ_d=d(1-q)^2 q^(d-1) and gain ratio Δ_(d+1)/Δ_d=q(d+1)/d. This yields strict concavity for q<1/2 and strict convexity for q>(m-2)/(m-1), hence unique balanced and concentrated degree multisets by elementary transfers; equality boundaries correctly allow ties. In the middle regime, an improving transfer excludes two degrees in [2,R], and another forces the high degrees >=R+1 to differ by ≤1; enumerating degree-one count, optional middle degree and high-degree floor yields all global maximizers among O(nm²) candidates. Cyclic primary-label block allocation realizes every legal degree sequence while covering every primary (E>=m). A uniform random extinction order and cut makes the removed count among d partners uniform 0..d, giving (d-1)/(d+1), whose discrete marginal is strictly decreasing. Independent Fraction-based enumeration confirmed 1,862 feasible (m,n,E,q) optimization instances including intermediate cases, ties and boundaries. The enumeration cannot replace the all-size transfers.

originality.rationale: Two-partner persistence differs from the all-neighbors-lost topological convention. The closest 2024 paper includes general threshold/hypergeometric survival probabilities but its degree-equality optimization in the inspected equations (8)-(13) is under the all-partners-lost assumption, not this two-survivor fixed-Bernoulli extinction objective. The mathematical boundary q=1/2 and q=(m-2)/(m-1), the intermediate normal form, and contrast with uniformly stage-averaged two-survivor robustness are not implied by that theorem. Abstract single-inflection allocation results or omitted supplements are residual risks.

value.rationale: Allocation of finite bipartite interaction budgets is natural in persistence/ecological-network design. The result identifies a true qualitative reversal between balanced and concentrated connections as species-extinction probability rises, gives exact constrained optimization beyond a few examples, and distinguishes snapshot survival from full-removal-trajectory robustness under the same two-partner rule. These are mathematically motivated phase boundaries, not arbitrary simulations.
